whatItFakes: Uses the median legal appointment deadline as appointment pacing.
why: A legal maximum is not an observed appointment duration; preserve the existing proxy.
replacement: Sourced appointment chronology or an approved pacing model.

whatItFakes: Every recorded partial executive tenure counts as a full term; missing end dates imply continuity.
why: The old checker does not implement jurisdiction-specific partial-service rules.
replacement: Dated partial-service counting facts selected by the caller.

whatItFakes: Every runoff finalist receives at least one permille of primary pull.
why: Legacy positive floor preserves otherwise zero-weight candidates.
replacement: Approved treatment of zero recorded primary support.

whatItFakes: Searches at most 16 past years for a regular executive term.
why: Legacy bounded search can reject a valid longer cycle.
replacement: Validated cycle bounds or a direct equivalent term calculation.

whatItFakes: 90 days determines whether executive terms are consecutive.
why: Legacy placeholder is not researched law.
replacement: Per-office dated consecutive-service rule.

whatItFakes: 365.25 days approximates every lookback year.
why: The legacy checker rounds this conversion instead of using legal anniversary dates.
replacement: Sourced lookback-date interpretation and calendar arithmetic.

whatItFakes: Incumbent 1.5, party-backed 1.25, other 1 determine primary support.
why: Hand-set standing estimates; preserve rather than recalibrate.
replacement: Evidence-based support factors admitted through the outcome-web port.

whatItFakes: Missing party share becomes 0.5.
why: The legacy tally fabricates a neutral share for missing district evidence.
replacement: Caller-supplied dated district shares with explicit missing-evidence policy.

whatItFakes: Every party receives at least 0.01 share in primary pull.
why: The positive floor can give entrants support despite recorded zero share.
replacement: Approved support model and zero-share semantics.

whatItFakes: Uses a common 55% two-party share to open self-starter consideration; missing shares count as zero.
why: Preserve the legacy field-recruitment gate; it does not decide whether the person runs.
replacement: Reviewed recruitment opportunity derived from supplied district facts with sourced calibration.

whatItFakes: One council ordinance per week before world opening determines the opening measure number.
why: Legacy has no measured council legislative-volume series; preserve numbering unchanged.
replacement: Recorded introduced-measure counts for the council and session.

whatItFakes: Empty or mismatched modal inputs can return undefined despite the declared T return type.
why: The unchanged legacy helper indexes values[best] without validating parallel input sizes. Preserve its missing-result behavior.
replacement: Reviewed explicit empty-result and parallel-array contract.

whatItFakes: An incumbent receives a 0.03 two-party share bonus.
why: Legacy aggregate election model, not a measured personal advantage.
replacement: Approved seat-specific incumbency model.

whatItFakes: Unresolved town dates use the profile weekday/parity and two-year cadence.
why: Published dates and fallback seasons retain their old cadence assumptions.
replacement: Sourced local election calendars.

whatItFakes: States without reviewed seat cycles use even-November profile calendars.
why: Legacy cohort fallback can flatten state-specific election days.
replacement: Complete sourced state seat calendars.

whatItFakes: Term changes defer immediate effects to regular terms and stop after 40 years.
why: Existing boundary and bounded search are preserved.
replacement: Admitted operative-date doctrine and unbounded validated cycle search.

whatItFakes: Unresolved council limits use two consecutive terms and a 31-day continuity gap.
why: The old council model supplies these defaults.
replacement: Sourced council partial-service and continuity rules.

whatItFakes: Legislative service spans use 31 days as continuity and 365.25 days per year.
why: Not a jurisdiction-specific statutory service convention.
replacement: Dated statutory service-counting rules.

whatItFakes: Opening service draws 0–13 years, caps by age/limits, and uses 365-day years.
why: Seeded creation of who exists is retained; not an actor decision roll.
replacement: Measured opening age and service distributions.

whatItFakes: State seats use pooled House logit spread, statewide Senate fallback, and rounded party ranks.
why: In-world projection preserves old district lean and party allocation assumptions.
replacement: Reviewed state district lean and party facts.

whatItFakes: A district without a recorded member count defaults to one seat.
why: The source catalog closure has this default.
replacement: Complete multi-member district counts.

whatItFakes: District electors follow statewide presidential votes, with missing shares 0.5 and counts zero.
why: Legacy missing-count and district proxies are preserved.
replacement: Certified district presidential tallies and complete state observations.

whatItFakes: Partial presidential service is compared against 365 times two days.
why: A leap year can differ from this fixed-day interpretation.
replacement: Calendar-based constitutional partial-term test.

whatItFakes: Any recorded death disqualifies a pending winner, even after the queried date.
why: Suspected legacy temporal bug is lifted unchanged.
replacement: CTO-approved dated alive check.

whatItFakes: Wake pack extraction considers every prefix preceding a pipe in event tags.
why: A broad prefix selector may include unrelated keys; preserved pending CTO review.
replacement: Validated pack-tag decoding.

whatItFakes: Statehood renewals stop after 200 iterations; multiple House seats reuse the same district key.
why: Guard and duplicate-key behavior are unchanged suspected limits.
replacement: Approved long-range renewal and distinct district identities.

whatItFakes: Opening bill counts spread annual introductions evenly over 365 days and use the lower median where absent.
why: Estimated opening pace is not a measured session chronology.
replacement: Dated bill-introduction chronology.

whatItFakes: Recorded eligible residents stand in for historical-election threshold denominators.
why: Legacy closure uses registered voters even when the filed base names an election.
replacement: Sourced historical vote denominator selected at filing.

whatItFakes: Missing primary method/date and runoff gaps use national modes and median filing gaps.
why: The complete legacy modal and fallback closure is preserved.
replacement: Complete sourced nomination calendars for each office.

whatItFakes: State turnover uses broad January/March/November windows and four previous years.
why: A cheap gate can suppress work outside those placeholder windows.
replacement: Verified exact due-event scheduling for every seat.

whatItFakes: Cycles after 2028 carry the 2020 census electoral allocation forward.
why: The existing allocation source is valid only for 2024 and 2028.
replacement: Sourced allocation for each reapportionment.

whatItFakes: Contingent ballots follow major-party affiliation/ticket index; Senate whole membership is twice the reference-state count, even if statehood adds seats.
why: Legacy bloc-voting and fixed-state denominators remain unchanged; added statehood seats can disagree with that denominator.
replacement: Individual recorded contingent ballots and current constitutional state/chamber membership.
